subject: Geography
topic: Biosphere reserves of India — mixed tiers
description: MAB programme, India's 18 reserves, UNESCO-recognised, key states + ecosystems

questions.stem: The concept of Biosphere Reserves is associated with which UNESCO programme?

options.option_text: Operation Tiger
Man and the Biosphere (MAB) Programme
World Heritage Programme
Ramsar Convention

questions.explanation: MAB (Man and the Biosphere) Programme — UNESCO, launched 1971. Biosphere Reserves are 'science for sustainability' sites — combining biodiversity conservation with sustainable use. Three zones: (1) CORE — strictly protected, no human disturbance; (2) BUFFER — limited research, education, eco-tourism; (3) TRANSITION — communities live and work, sustainable practices. India has 18 designated biosphere reserves (national list); 12 of them are also part of the UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reserves (WNBR). India joined WNBR with Nilgiri (2000).

questions.stem: India's FIRST Biosphere Reserve, designated in 1986, is:

options.option_text: Nanda Devi
Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve (Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka)
Sundarbans
Great Nicobar

questions.explanation: Nilgiri — 1st BR, designated 1 Sep 1986. Spans Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka (parts of all three). Includes Bandipur, Mudumalai, Nagarhole, Mukurthi NPs and Wayanad WLS, Silent Valley NP. Ecologically rich — Western Ghats endemics (Lion-tailed macaque, Nilgiri tahr, Nilgiri langur). UNESCO WNBR 2000. Often confused with Nanda Devi (designated 1988, 2nd BR). Sequence of first 5 Indian BRs: Nilgiri (1986), Nanda Devi (1988), Nokrek (1988), Manas (1989), Sundarbans (1989).

questions.stem: The COLD DESERT Biosphere Reserve, located in Himachal Pradesh, includes which national park?

options.option_text: Hemis (in Ladakh)
Pin Valley National Park (Lahaul & Spiti)
Great Himalayan National Park
Khangchendzonga

questions.explanation: Cold Desert Biosphere Reserve — designated 2009; covers Pin Valley NP, Chandratal + Sarchu wetlands, Kibber WLS in the Lahaul & Spiti district of Himachal Pradesh. Habitat of the elusive snow leopard (Pin Valley). Hemis NP — in Ladakh, separate (largest NP in India by area, ~4,400 km²; not in HP). Khangchendzonga — Sikkim BR (UNESCO 2018, also a World Heritage Site). India's 18 BRs by approximate region: Western Ghats (4 — Nilgiri, Agasthyamala, NBR core, Gulf of Mannar coastal); Eastern Himalaya (4 — Nanda Devi, Khangchendzonga, Nokrek, Dibru-Saikhowa); NE (2 — Manas, Dehang Dibang); Central India (3 — Achanakmar-Amarkantak, Pachmarhi, Panna); Coastal/Islands (2 — Great Nicobar, Sundarbans); Cold Desert (1 — HP); Salt-marsh (1 — Kachchh, Gujarat); Aravalli (1 — Pachpadra/Sariska area as proposed) — totals approximate.

questions.stem: The Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve, India's first MARINE biosphere reserve, lies along which coast?

options.option_text: Coast of Gujarat
Coast of Tamil Nadu (between India and Sri Lanka)
Coast of Odisha
Andaman & Nicobar Islands

questions.explanation: Gulf of Mannar BR — declared 1989; India's FIRST marine BR. Stretches ~140 km along Tamil Nadu coast from Rameswaram in the north to Kanyakumari in the south. 21 small islands; ~3,600 km² of coral reefs, mangroves, seagrass beds, salt marshes. Habitat of dugong (sea cow — endangered), corals, sacred chank, dolphins. UNESCO WNBR 2001. The Kachchh BR (Gulf of Kutch — 2008) is in Gujarat. Bhitarkanika in Odisha is a notable mangrove + olive ridley site but a Ramsar site / NP, not a BR.

questions.stem: Which biosphere reserve, located in Madhya Pradesh, was added to the UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reserves in 2009 and contains the Bori sanctuary, Pachmarhi and Satpura NPs?

options.option_text: Achanakmar-Amarkantak
Pachmarhi Biosphere Reserve
Panna Biosphere Reserve
Kanha-Pench corridor

questions.explanation: Pachmarhi BR — Madhya Pradesh, designated 1999; UNESCO WNBR 2009. Includes Pachmarhi NP, Bori WLS, Satpura NP. Located on the Satpura range; rich in deciduous forests, gorges, waterfalls (Bee Falls, Apsara Vihar). 'Queen of Satpuras' — Pachmarhi hill station. Achanakmar-Amarkantak BR — straddles MP + Chhattisgarh, includes the source of Narmada. Panna BR — MP, around Panna Tiger Reserve. Kanha-Pench — separate tiger reserves (not a single BR).

questions.stem: The largest biosphere reserve in India by area is the:

options.option_text: Nilgiri
Gulf of Kachchh BR
Cold Desert BR (~7,770 km², Lahaul-Spiti, Himachal Pradesh)
Sundarbans

questions.explanation: Cold Desert BR — ~7,770 km², largest in India by area. Spans Lahaul-Spiti and Kinnaur districts of HP. Other large BRs: Gulf of Kachchh (~7,506 km²), Sundarbans (~9,630 km² — actually slightly larger than Cold Desert depending on the boundary delineation; both are sometimes quoted as #1). Smallest BR — Dibru-Saikhowa (~765 km², Assam). 18 BRs total; 12 of them in UNESCO WNBR. Most recent UNESCO addition — Panna (2020). Note: the area-ranking order shifts with revised boundary maps; the conventional answer for 'largest' is the Cold Desert / Gulf of Kachchh in older sources and Sundarbans in newer reckonings.

questions.stem: Which UNESCO-recognised Biosphere Reserve in the Northeast spans Sikkim and shares its territory with the world's third-highest mountain peak?

options.option_text: Manas
Khangchendzonga (Kanchenjunga) Biosphere Reserve, Sikkim
Nokrek (Meghalaya)
Dibru-Saikhowa (Assam)

questions.explanation: Khangchendzonga BR — Sikkim. UNESCO WNBR 2018. Surrounds Mt Kanchenjunga (8,586 m, world's 3rd highest peak — India's highest peak; on India-Nepal border). The Khangchendzonga National Park within it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (Mixed natural + cultural, 2016) — recognising both biodiversity (snow leopard, red panda, blue sheep) and the mountain's sacred status to the Lepcha people. Manas BR — Assam, royal Bengal tiger + golden langur + pygmy hog + hispid hare, also a UNESCO World Heritage Site (1985, originally listed as 'in danger' due to insurgency, removed from danger list in 2011). Nokrek — Meghalaya, citrus genetic diversity centre. Dibru-Saikhowa — Assam, river-island ecosystem.

questions.stem: The Nokrek Biosphere Reserve in Meghalaya is internationally recognised as the gene sanctuary of which plant group?

options.option_text: Wild paddy (ancestral varieties of Oryza sativa)
Wild citrus (ancestral relatives of oranges and lemons)
Wild banana (origin of Musa species cultivated today)
Wild cardamom (primary genetic reserve of Elettaria)

questions.explanation: Nokrek harbours Citrus indica, the wild progenitor of cultivated citrus fruits such as oranges and lemons, earning it recognition as a global citrus gene sanctuary under UNESCO MAB. Wild paddy gene diversity is associated with Jeypore Tract in Odisha, not Nokrek, making Option A the most tempting wrong choice.

questions.stem: The Sundarbans Biosphere Reserve, renowned for its Royal Bengal Tiger population in mangrove habitats, lies entirely within which Indian state?

options.option_text: Odisha — home to the Bhitarkanika mangrove ecosystem
Andhra Pradesh — along the Krishna and Godavari delta
West Bengal — covering part of the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta
Tamil Nadu — bordering the Palk Strait and Bay of Bengal

questions.explanation: The Indian portion of the Sundarbans Biosphere Reserve falls entirely in West Bengal, covering the world's largest mangrove delta shared with Bangladesh. Odisha is a common distractor because Bhitarkanika is also a notable mangrove-based wildlife sanctuary, but it is not the Sundarbans BR.

questions.stem: Achanakmar-Amarkantak Biosphere Reserve, inscribed in the UNESCO World Network in 2012, straddles which pair of Indian states?

options.option_text: Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra, sharing the Satpura Hills
Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand, along the eastern plateau rim
Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh, along the Vindhya range
Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh, covering the Maikal Hills

questions.explanation: Achanakmar-Amarkantak BR spans Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh across the Maikal Hills and the Amarkantak plateau, which is the source of the Narmada and Son rivers. Option C (MP and UP) is the most common distractor because Amarkantak is near the Vindhyan foothills, but Uttar Pradesh is not part of this reserve.

questions.stem: Dibru-Saikhowa Biosphere Reserve is ecologically notable for harbouring a population of semi-wild feral horses. In which state is it located?

options.option_text: Assam, on the floodplains of the upper Brahmaputra valley
Arunachal Pradesh, within the Eastern Himalayan foothills
Meghalaya, in the sub-Himalayan foothills near Garo Hills
Manipur, covering the Indo-Burma biodiversity hotspot zone

questions.explanation: Dibru-Saikhowa Biosphere Reserve lies in the upper Brahmaputra floodplains of Assam and is uniquely known for feral horses descended from military horses abandoned after World War II. Arunachal Pradesh is a frequent distractor because the reserve sits at the Assam–Arunachal border, but the BR itself is administratively in Assam.

questions.stem: Agasthyamalai Biosphere Reserve, designated a UNESCO World Network site in 2016, is spread across which two Indian states?

options.option_text: Goa and Karnataka, along the northern Western Ghats spine
Karnataka and Kerala, forming the central Ghats corridor
Kerala and Tamil Nadu, at the southern tip of Western Ghats
Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh, in the Eastern Ghats region

questions.explanation: Agasthyamalai (Agasthyamala) BR covers the southernmost extension of the Western Ghats in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, encompassing Neyyar, Peppara, and Shendurney wildlife sanctuaries. Karnataka–Kerala (Option B) is the most tempting distractor because both share the Western Ghats, but Agasthyamalai is specifically in the Kerala–Tamil Nadu section.

questions.stem: Under the UNESCO MAB three-zone model, the outermost zone of a biosphere reserve — where permanent human settlements, traditional farming, and sustainable tourism are formally permitted — is called the:

options.option_text: Buffer zone — for research, education, and limited controlled access
Core zone — strictly protected with no permanent human habitation
Transition zone — sustainable use area with human communities present
Rehabilitation zone — for ecological restoration of degraded patches

questions.explanation: The MAB model zones outward as Core (strict protection) → Buffer (research/education/limited tourism) → Transition (also called Cooperation zone), where permanent settlements and sustainable economic activities are permitted. Option A (buffer zone) is the strongest distractor because tourists often enter there, but it does NOT permit permanent settlements. 'Rehabilitation zone' (Option D) has no place in the standard MAB framework.

questions.stem: Which biosphere reserve was most recently inscribed in the UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reserves as of 2020, bringing India's total in the WNBR to twelve?

options.option_text: Khangchendzonga, Sikkim — inscribed at the 2018 MAB ICC session
Panna, Madhya Pradesh — inscribed at the 2020 MAB ICC session
Simlipal, Odisha — inscribed at the 2009 MAB ICC session
Agasthyamalai, Kerala–Tamil Nadu — inscribed at the 2016 MAB session

questions.explanation: Panna Biosphere Reserve (Madhya Pradesh) was inscribed in the UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reserves in 2020, making it India's 12th and most recent WNBR site as of that year. Khangchendzonga (2018) is the most common wrong answer because it is the penultimate addition and many candidates conflate the two; Panna is also known as a successful tiger reintroduction site, adding to its distinctiveness.
